docs.quickstart.title: Quick Start
docs.quickstart.subtitle: Get your domain up and running in 3 steps.
docs.quickstart.step1.title: 1. Check availability
docs.quickstart.step1.desc: Go to the homepage and type your desired subdomain. We'll check all managed domains and tell you instantly if it's available.
docs.quickstart.step2.title: 2. Create your record
docs.quickstart.step2.desc: Sign up, log in, and click "Create" on an available domain. Choose your record type (A or CNAME) and enter the target. Your record is written to the nameserver immediately.
docs.quickstart.step3.title: 3. Manage from dashboard
docs.quickstart.step3.desc: Head to "My Domains" to update targets or remove records anytime. All changes sync to DNS automatically.
docs.quickstart.tip: DNS changes typically propagate worldwide within 5 minutes.
docs.vercel.title: Vercel Setup
docs.vercel.subtitle: Connect your Sitey domain to a Vercel project.
docs.vercel.step1.title: 1. Add domain in Vercel
docs.vercel.step1.desc: In your Vercel project settings, add your custom domain.
docs.vercel.step1.item1: Go to your Vercel project → Settings → Domains.
docs.vercel.step1.item2: Enter your Sitey domain (e.g. myapp.sitey.one) and click Add.
docs.vercel.step1.item3: Vercel will show you the required CNAME value (usually cname.vercel-dns.com).
docs.vercel.step2.title: 2. Create CNAME record on Sitey
docs.vercel.step2.desc: Back on Sitey, create a CNAME record pointing to Vercel.
docs.vercel.step2.item1: Search for your domain on the Sitey homepage and click Create.
docs.vercel.step2.item3: Enter the value Vercel gave you (e.g. cname.vercel-dns.com).
docs.vercel.step3.title: 3. Add TXT verification
docs.vercel.step3.desc: Vercel may require a TXT record to verify domain ownership.
docs.vercel.step3.item1: In your Sitey dashboard, find your domain and expand it.
docs.vercel.step3.item2: You'll see a "Vercel TXT Verification" field below the CNAME value.
docs.vercel.step3.item3: Paste the verification value from Vercel (e.g. vc-domain-verify=...) and click Save.
docs.vercel.tip: After setup, Vercel will automatically provision an SSL certificate. This usually takes a few minutes.
docs.records.title: Record Types
docs.records.subtitle: Learn about the DNS record types Sitey supports.
docs.records.a.title: A Record
docs.records.a.desc: An A record maps your domain directly to an IPv4 address. Use this when you have a server with a static IP.
docs.records.cname.title: CNAME Record
docs.records.cname.desc: A CNAME record maps your domain to another hostname. Use this for services like Vercel, Netlify, or GitHub Pages that give you a hostname instead of an IP.
docs.records.txt.title: TXT Record (Vercel verification)
docs.records.txt.desc: TXT records are used for domain verification. When connecting to Vercel, you may need to add a TXT record to prove you own the domain. You can manage this from the dashboard when editing a CNAME record.

blog.title: 100+ Domain Name Ideas for Developers in 2026
blog.meta: A curated list of short, memorable subdomain names you can claim right now — free.
blog.intro: Finding the perfect domain name is half the battle when launching a project. We picked 100+ short, memorable names that work great as subdomains. Click any name to check if it's available — you can grab it in seconds, no registrar needed.
blog.why.title: Why domain names matter
blog.why.body: A good domain name is short, memorable, and hints at what you do. Here are a few rules we follow:
blog.why.tip1.title: Keep it short
blog.why.tip1.desc: Under 10 characters is ideal. Easy to type, easy to remember, easy to share.
blog.why.tip2.title: Easy to spell
blog.why.tip2.desc: Avoid numbers, hyphens, or tricky spellings. If you need to clarify it over the phone, it's too hard.
blog.why.tip3.title: Memorable
blog.why.tip3.desc: Pick a name with personality. Generic words get forgotten quickly.
blog.why.tip4.title: Relevant
blog.why.tip4.desc: Hint at what your project does. "blog.sitey.one" beats "stuff.sitey.one".
blog.portfolio.title: Portfolio & Personal
